sections.title: What you know
sections.content: You know *negar que*, *desmentir que* and *no negar que* from B2 Unit 5, and *negarse a* from B1 Unit 40. You know *admitir* from B1 Unit 21, *reconocer* from B1 Unit 7, and the rule "same person: infinitive" from B2 Unit 4. In a dispute there are two sides: those who reject a claim (*negar*, *desmentir*, *contradecir*) and those who accept it (*admitir*, *reconocer*). This lesson reports both.

sections.title: Denying and admitting
rows: negar que + pluperfect subjunctive (a past action)
Admitió que había cometido un error.

sections.title: The same fact from both sides
sections.content: The same fact can be reported from both sides. «Fui yo» becomes *Admitió que había sido él* or *Admitió haberlo hecho*. «No fui yo» becomes *Negó que hubiera sido él* or *Negó haberlo hecho*. When the person who denies or admits is also the person who acted, the infinitive with *haber* is the natural choice, just as with the verbs of B2 Unit 4. When someone else acted, use *que*: *Negó que su hermano lo hubiera hecho*. *Contradecir* takes the person as its object: *Me contradijo* (He contradicted me).

items.spanish: Luis negó que Ana hubiera llegado tarde.
items.english: Luis denied that Ana had arrived late.

items.spanish: Meg negó haber visto el mensaje.
items.english: Meg denied having seen the message.

items.spanish: Carlos admitió que había hecho el trabajo.
items.english: Carlos admitted that he had done the work.

items.spanish: Ana replicó que ya había avisado a todos.
items.english: Ana answered back that she had already told everyone.

sections.content: Choose the verb first, then the mood: rejecting (*negar*, *desmentir*) takes the subjunctive, accepting (*admitir*, *reconocer*) and answering back (*replicar*, *objetar*) take the indicative. With the same person, use *haber* + participle.
